claims.text: Treating a Pulumi Output<T> as a plain value can produce placeholder text such as `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` in log lines, generated files, or resource properties.
The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ ('Output value errors') exists and describes this and other symptoms of treating an output as if it were already a plain value.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ covering errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value like a plain value.
Pulumi CLI/Cloud returns a "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" error when another update is in progress.
Pulumi Cloud can return 500 internal server errors.
The Pulumi CLI emits a `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` error when it cannot access a self-managed (DIY) state backend.
On Apple Silicon, running x86_64 binaries under Rosetta 2 can cause Pulumi crashes or hangs.
A recently deleted stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
Pulumi supports limiting operations to specific resources with the `--target` and `--exclude` flags.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
Pulumi dev builds provide pre-release builds with bug fixes not yet shipped in a stable release.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the providing resource has been created or updated.

Converting a Pulumi output value to a string directly (without apply or an equivalent helper) does not raise an error by default; Pulumi silently substitutes a placeholder message in place of the value.

In Pulumi TypeScript, the resulting string from string-converting an Output contains text such as `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`.
In Pulumi TypeScript, calling `JSON.stringify()` on an output produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.
In Pulumi Python, using an Output in an f-string produces a string containing `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported`, and Pulumi also logs a warning; no exception is raised.
In Pulumi Python, passing an output to `json.dumps()` fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`.
In Pulumi Python, `Output.json_dumps()` is the way to serialize outputs to JSON.
In Go, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error.
In Pulumi Go, output values are resolved with `ApplyT`.
In Pulumi C#, string-converting an Output produces text such as `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`.

Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` (supported in TypeScript, Python, and C#) makes converting an output to a string throw an exception instead of returning placeholder text.

The string-composition helpers are `pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` in TypeScript, `Output.concat`/`Output.format`/`Output.json_dumps` in Python, `pulumi.Sprintf`/`pulumi.JSONMarshal` in Go, and `Output.Format` in C#.

A value read inside an `apply` callback is only available inside that callback; the callback runs asynchronously, generally after the program's top-level code has finished, so an outer variable assigned within it is still undefined when read outside.
The apply callback runs when the engine resolves the dependency graph, so adding a delay does not fix reading the value outside the callback.
Most Pulumi resource inputs accept outputs as well as plain values, but a handful of positions, such as a resource's logical name, cannot.
In a dynamically typed language, an `if` on a Pulumi output evaluates the output object rather than its eventual value, so it is generally always true.
In a statically typed language, branching on an `Output<bool>` is usually a compile error because an `Output<bool>` is not a `bool`.
Values known when the program starts, such as stack configuration read with `pulumi.Config`, environment variables, or hardcoded flags, are plain values and can be branched on normally.
Passing an output as a resource logical name, loop bound, or map key fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#, where these positions are typed as plain strings or numbers.
In Pulumi Python, passing an output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Python, using a Pulumi output as a loop bound (`range(some_output)`) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Python, using a Pulumi output as a dictionary key does not raise an error; it silently keys on the output object itself.
Resources whose names or counts depend on values known only after another resource is provisioned can be moved to a separate stack that consumes the first stack's outputs through a StackReference.

Pulumi has no supported way to block the program and read a resolved output value synchronously; awaiting or synchronously reading an output either doesn't compile, fails at runtime, or returns placeholder text.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output from the CLI after a deployment.
A StackReference lets one Pulumi program consume another stack's outputs as inputs.
The Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (e.g. `res.Outputs` in Go).
